meta.method: Perplexity API, model sonar-pro (standard search, not deep research), 18 queries; Kling camera list verified on kling.ai; Veo primary pages could not be rendered so Veo claims are secondary-sourced; prompt_phrase and ai_risk are planner judgement synthesised from the cited vendor guides and have not been tested by generating video.
meta.risk_levels: low = reliable, medium = works with care, high = frequently fails

angles.name: Eye level
angles.what_it_is: Camera at the subject's eye height, looking straight on.
angles.emotion: Neutral, natural, equal footing with the character.
angles.use_when: Ordinary dialogue, exposition, realistic drama, product demos needing credibility.
angles.prompt_phrase: eye-level shot, camera at the subject's eye height

ai_risk.note: Safest default; reliable in every model.

angles.name: Low angle
angles.what_it_is: Camera below the eye line, looking up.
angles.use_when: Hero entrances, villains, leaders, aspirational brand moments.
angles.prompt_phrase: low-angle shot looking up at the subject

ai_risk.note: Works as a framing cue in Veo and Kling guides; very low angles can stretch limbs and faces.

angles.name: High angle
angles.what_it_is: Camera above the subject, looking down.
angles.use_when: Loss of control, being cornered, a character alone in a big space.
angles.prompt_phrase: high-angle shot looking down at the subject

ai_risk.note: Reliable framing cue.

angles.name: Bird's-eye / overhead
angles.what_it_is: Camera very high, looking straight or nearly straight down.
angles.use_when: Choreography, geography, food or product flat-lays, isolation.
angles.prompt_phrase: overhead top-down shot looking straight down

ai_risk.note: Top-down framing is understood, but perspective on people can look flattened or limbs odd; keep subjects simple.

angles.name: Worm's-eye
angles.what_it_is: Camera at ground level, looking sharply upward.
angles.use_when: Buildings, giants, monsters, a sudden sense of enormity.
angles.prompt_phrase: worm's-eye view from ground level looking steeply up

ai_risk.note: Extreme perspective distorts bodies; the term is less common in guides, so pair with 'camera on the ground, looking up'.

angles.name: Dutch / canted
angles.what_it_is: Camera tilted so the horizon runs diagonal.
angles.use_when: Panic, intoxication, danger, reality breaking down. Use sparingly.
angles.prompt_phrase: dutch angle, camera tilted so the horizon is diagonal

ai_risk.note: Model may tilt the whole scene inconsistently or drift back to level mid-clip; keep the clip short and static.

angles.name: Over-the-shoulder
angles.what_it_is: Camera behind one character, their shoulder and head in the foreground, looking at another.
angles.prompt_phrase: over-the-shoulder shot from behind her left shoulder, facing him

ai_risk.note: Models often drop the foreground shoulder, merge the two heads, or flip who faces whom. Generate from a reference still.

angles.name: POV
angles.what_it_is: Camera shows exactly what a character sees.
angles.use_when: Searching, stalking, reading a message, looking through binoculars.
angles.prompt_phrase: first-person point-of-view shot, seen through the character's eyes

ai_risk.note: Works when hands or the object are all that appear; showing the viewer's own body adds hand errors.

angles.name: Aerial / drone
angles.what_it_is: Camera airborne, travelling above a scene.
angles.use_when: Establishing a city or landscape, connecting locations, following a vehicle.
angles.prompt_phrase: aerial drone shot high above, slowly moving forward

ai_risk.note: Landscape scale is a model strength, but fast forward flight warps terrain and buildings; keep it slow.

shot_types.name: Extreme wide / establishing
shot_types.what_it_is: Subject tiny in a vast environment; shows the whole location.
shot_types.use_when: Opening a scene, changing location, showing scale.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: extreme wide establishing shot, tiny figure in a vast landscape

ai_risk.note: Models handle environments well; faces at this size are soft, so avoid needing identity here.

shot_types.name: Wide
shot_types.use_when: Scene geography, entrances, blocking, movement through space.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: wide shot showing the full room and the characters within it

ai_risk.note: Small faces can drift between frames; keep action simple.

shot_types.name: Full shot
shot_types.what_it_is: Entire body head to toe, little spare space.
shot_types.emotion: Physical presence, clarity of posture and costume.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: full-body shot, head to toe in frame

ai_risk.note: Feet and legs are a common failure point (sliding, extra limbs).

shot_types.name: Cowboy / medium wide
shot_types.what_it_is: Subject framed from about mid-thigh up.
shot_types.use_when: Standoffs, entrances, scenes needing both hands and face.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: cowboy shot, framed from mid-thigh up

ai_risk.note: Term 'cowboy shot' is understood; if not, say 'framed from the thighs up'.

shot_types.name: Medium
shot_types.emotion: Neutral, conversational; balances face and body.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: medium shot, framed from the waist up

ai_risk.note: Most reliable human framing.

shot_types.name: Medium close-up
shot_types.prompt_phrase: medium close-up, framed from the chest up

ai_risk.note: Reliable; face detail good.

shot_types.name: Close-up
shot_types.what_it_is: Face or key object fills the frame.
shot_types.use_when: Decisions, grief, fear, emotional turns; product hero.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: close-up on the face, shallow depth of field

ai_risk.note: Best identity fidelity, which is why AI over-produces it; plan it as the exception.

shot_types.name: Extreme close-up
shot_types.what_it_is: Isolated small detail: eyes, lips, hand, key.
shot_types.use_when: Micro-expressions, clues, a trigger pull. Rare.

ai_risk.note: Eyes and teeth can deform; hands in close-up add finger errors.

shot_types.name: Insert / detail
shot_types.what_it_is: Brief close-up of an object or action cut into a scene.
shot_types.use_when: Letter, ring, phone screen, hands on a tool.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: insert shot of a hand placing the key on the table, macro detail

ai_risk.note: Readable text on objects will garble; generate screens and labels in post.

shot_types.name: Two-shot
shot_types.prompt_phrase: two-shot, both characters in frame, medium distance

ai_risk.note: Two faces drift or merge across a clip; keep both still and facing.

shot_types.name: Group shot
shot_types.what_it_is: Three or more people framed together.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: group shot, five people around a table, wide medium framing

ai_risk.note: Identity and count drift; faces beyond two or three degrade quickly.

shot_types.name: Master shot
shot_types.what_it_is: Wide shot covering the whole scene's action.
shot_types.use_when: Start of a scene and every return-to-orientation moment.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: master shot, wide static view of the whole scene

ai_risk.note: Simple, static wide; good AI target.

shot_types.name: Cutaway
shot_types.what_it_is: Shot of something else related to the scene.
shot_types.use_when: Show what a character notices, bridge edits, hide a continuity issue.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: cutaway to the clock on the wall, static

ai_risk.note: Easy; no character identity needed.

shot_types.name: Reaction shot
shot_types.what_it_is: Character responding to what was said or seen.
shot_types.use_when: After news, a joke, a threat, a revelation.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: reaction shot, close-up of her face as she realizes, subtle change of expression

ai_risk.note: Expression changes can look uncanny; ask for one small change.

shot_types.name: Reverse / shot-reverse-shot
shot_types.what_it_is: Opposite viewpoint; alternating shots of two people facing each other.
shot_types.prompt_phrase: reverse angle from the other character's side, matching eyeline

ai_risk.note: Model has no memory of the first clip; the room and the person must be re-specified identically.

moves.name: Static / locked off
moves.what_it_is: Camera fixed on a tripod.
moves.use_when: Performance, tense dialogue, any shot where fidelity matters most.
moves.prompt_phrase: static camera, locked-off shot, no camera movement

ai_risk.note: Most stable output; default for the majority of shots.

moves.name: Zoom in
moves.what_it_is: Lens focal length increases; camera stays put.
moves.emotion: Attention, scrutiny, emphasis; fast zoom feels TV-like.
moves.use_when: Isolate a detail without entering the space.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow zoom in on the subject

ai_risk.note: Often confused with push-in; say 'zoom' only if you want flat optical magnification.

moves.name: Zoom out
moves.what_it_is: Lens focal length decreases; camera stays put.
moves.use_when: Reveal that a character is alone or surrounded.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow zoom out revealing the surroundings

ai_risk.note: New background must be invented; keep slow.

moves.name: Dolly in
moves.what_it_is: Camera physically moves toward the subject on a dolly.
moves.use_when: Character understands something; rising tension.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow dolly in toward the subject

ai_risk.note: One of the best-supported moves; Kling guide says plain 'camera slowly moves closer' may work better than the word dolly.

moves.name: Dolly out
moves.what_it_is: Camera physically moves away from the subject.
moves.use_when: Pull away after bad news; reveal the larger room.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow dolly out, pulling back from the subject

ai_risk.note: Revealed background is invented; keep slow.

moves.name: Push-in
moves.what_it_is: Deliberate advance toward a subject (usually a dolly in; also slider or gimbal).
moves.use_when: Internal turning point; information becomes important.
moves.prompt_phrase: gentle push-in toward the subject's face

ai_risk.note: Preferred term across Kling and MiniMax docs; treated like dolly in by Veo guides.

moves.name: Pull-out
moves.what_it_is: Camera moves backward away from the subject.
moves.use_when: Leave a character small in a big space.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow pull-out, camera retreats from the subject

ai_risk.note: Same as dolly out.

moves.name: Tracking / follow
moves.what_it_is: Camera travels with a moving subject at similar distance.
moves.use_when: Walk-and-talk, runner, a journey in real time.
moves.prompt_phrase: smooth tracking shot following the subject from behind

ai_risk.note: Best for slow or medium subject speed; running or fast turns cause leg and background warping.

moves.name: Truck (lateral)
moves.what_it_is: Camera moves sideways, parallel to the subject.
moves.emotion: Kinetic discovery, moving through a space.
moves.use_when: Reveal items along a wall; walk beside a character.
moves.prompt_phrase: camera trucks left, sideways move, parallax in the foreground

ai_risk.note: Lateral parallax is well supported; MiniMax has an explicit tag.

moves.name: Pan
moves.what_it_is: Camera rotates horizontally from a fixed point.
moves.use_when: Survey a space; follow action; link two subjects.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow pan from left to right

ai_risk.note: Slow pans are reliable.

moves.name: Tilt
moves.what_it_is: Camera rotates vertically from a fixed point.
moves.use_when: Feet to skyline; reveal height or status.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow tilt up from the street to the top of the building

ai_risk.note: Reliable when slow.

moves.name: Whip pan
moves.what_it_is: Very fast pan with heavy motion blur.
moves.use_when: Transition between two shots or two places.
moves.prompt_phrase: (do not use in one clip; build as two clips joined by a blur transition)

ai_risk.note: Smears, geometry collapse, subject vanishing. Fake it in the edit.

moves.name: Panoramic / sweeping pan
moves.what_it_is: Wide, slow horizontal scan across a landscape or room.
moves.use_when: Establishing geography.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow panoramic pan across the landscape

ai_risk.note: Long pans invent a lot of new scene; keep under about 90 degrees.

moves.name: Crane / jib up or down
moves.what_it_is: Camera rises or descends, often with a diagonal sweep.
moves.emotion: Grandeur, release, shift from intimate to expansive.
moves.use_when: Reveal a crowd or landscape; end a scene by lifting away.
moves.prompt_phrase: crane up, rising slowly to reveal the whole scene

ai_risk.note: Supported by Veo guides; the revealed area is invented, keep it simple.

moves.name: Handheld
moves.what_it_is: Operator-carried camera with small irregular shake.
moves.use_when: Chases, emergencies, intimate or chaotic scenes.
moves.prompt_phrase: subtle handheld camera, slight natural shake

ai_risk.note: Too much shake blurs identity; say 'subtle'.

moves.name: Steadicam
moves.what_it_is: Body-stabilised camera: floating, level walking move.
moves.use_when: Follow through corridors, crowds, stairs.
moves.prompt_phrase: smooth steadicam follow shot, floating stabilised motion

ai_risk.note: Treat as tracking; long corridors accumulate errors.

moves.name: Orbit / arc
moves.what_it_is: Camera circles around the subject.
moves.use_when: Hero product, kiss, confrontation, pivotal beat.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow half-orbit around the subject, counterclockwise

ai_risk.note: Needs consistent 3D from changing angles; use a half-orbit at most, simple subject, clear background.

moves.name: Dolly zoom (vertigo)
moves.what_it_is: Camera moves one way while lens zooms the opposite way; subject size constant, background stretches or squeezes.
moves.use_when: Realisation or shock. Once per piece at most.
moves.prompt_phrase: dolly zoom vertigo effect, background stretching behind a steady subject

ai_risk.note: Model often renders a plain zoom or push; unreliable.

moves.name: Rack focus
moves.what_it_is: Focus shifts between depth planes mid-shot.
moves.use_when: Background clue becomes important; look from A to B.
moves.prompt_phrase: rack focus from the foreground object to the face in the background

ai_risk.note: Often yields a crossfade of blur instead of a clean shift; keep depth separation obvious.

moves.name: Reveal
moves.what_it_is: Move or composition change that uncovers hidden information.
moves.use_when: Show what was hidden: tilt up, pull back, pan past a foreground object.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow pull-back to reveal the vast scene

ai_risk.note: Combine with a single move only (pull back or tilt).

moves.name: Slow motion
moves.what_it_is: Action played slower than real time.
moves.use_when: Impact, falls, athletic moves, memory.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow motion, high frame rate look

ai_risk.note: Models vary; phrase as 'slow motion' and keep action simple.

moves.name: Time-lapse
moves.what_it_is: Frames far apart played fast.
moves.use_when: Sunrise, traffic, construction, seasons.
moves.prompt_phrase: time-lapse of clouds moving across the sky

ai_risk.note: Environment-only works well; with people, bodies jitter.

moves.name: Drone fly-over
moves.what_it_is: Aerial camera travelling over a place.
moves.use_when: Open a story; connect places.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow aerial drone fly-over, forward motion over the landscape

ai_risk.note: Fast flight warps terrain; keep slow.

moves.name: Pedestal up/down
moves.what_it_is: Camera rises or lowers vertically, no tilt.
moves.use_when: Vertical reveal in an interior.
moves.prompt_phrase: camera pedestals up smoothly, no tilt

ai_risk.note: MiniMax has a native tag; others use 'camera rises'.

moves.name: Dolly in
moves.what_it_is: Signature dolly: camera physically pushes toward the subject on a dolly track, so the foreground slides past and the background grows (real parallax, not lens magnification).
moves.emotion: Involvement, intimacy, dawning realisation, encroaching threat.
moves.use_when: Open a scene on the subject; a character understands something; tension rises before a turn.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow dolly in toward the subject, camera physically moving closer, parallax in the foreground

ai_risk.note: Reliable. Keep to one slow push. Faces can morph as the camera closes and scale can drift on the approach, so stop before a tight close-up. Kling may prefer the plain words 'camera slowly moves closer' over the word dolly. One camera move per clip only; do not stack a pan or zoom onto the same clip.

preset.label: OPEN_DOLLY_IN
preset.prompt: slow dolly in toward the subject, camera physically moving closer, parallax in the foreground, one camera move only

moves.name: Dolly out
moves.what_it_is: Signature dolly: camera physically pulls back from the subject along a dolly track, opening up the surrounding space (parallax reveals what was off-frame).
moves.emotion: Withdrawal, loneliness, scale, context revealed after a beat.
moves.use_when: Pull away after bad news; close a scene by leaving the subject; reveal the larger room.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow dolly out, camera physically pulling back from the subject, room revealed around them

ai_risk.note: The newly revealed background is invented and can morph as it appears; distance errors skew scale while pulling back. Keep it slow and the environment simple. One camera move per clip only.

preset.label: CLOSE_DOLLY_OUT
preset.prompt: slow dolly out, camera physically pulling back from the subject, simple room revealed, one camera move only

moves.name: Dolly and track
moves.what_it_is: Signature dolly: camera rides a dolly alongside or behind a moving subject, holding distance while the background slides past (a travelling two-in-one that still counts as a single camera move).
moves.emotion: Momentum, journey, being carried along with the subject.
moves.use_when: A walk-and-talk or a character moving through a space during an opening or a transition.
moves.prompt_phrase: camera on a dolly tracking alongside the walking subject, smooth steady move, background sliding past

ai_risk.note: Best at slow or medium subject speed; running or sharp turns morph legs and smear the background, and distance errors skew scale. Keep the single move steady; one camera move per clip only.

preset.label: TRANSITION_DOLLY_TRACK
preset.prompt: camera on a dolly tracking alongside the walking subject, smooth steady move, one camera move only

moves.name: Dolly zoom
moves.what_it_is: Signature dolly (vertigo): camera dollies one way while the lens zooms the opposite way, holding the subject at constant size while the background stretches or squeezes. The dolly changes parallax; only the zoom changes the lens.
moves.emotion: Dread, vertigo, the floor dropping out, reality shifting under a character.
moves.use_when: A single realisation or shock beat. Once per piece at most, never on dialogue.
moves.prompt_phrase: dolly zoom vertigo effect, camera dollying in while the lens zooms out, background stretching behind a steady subject

ai_risk.note: Models frequently collapse this into a plain zoom or a plain push; subject scale can also drift or morph when the two axes fight. Unreliable. The dolly-vs-zoom split is exactly what breaks here, so test per model before relying on it. One camera move per clip only; never a fast one.

preset.label: BEAT_DOLLY_ZOOM
preset.prompt: dolly zoom vertigo effect, camera dollying in while the lens zooms out, background stretching behind a steady subject, slow, one camera move only

moves.name: Lateral truck
moves.what_it_is: Signature dolly: camera trucks sideways on a dolly, parallel to the subject, sliding past foreground objects so parallax reads as depth.
moves.emotion: Kinetic discovery, moving through a space, items unveiling left to right.
moves.use_when: Reveal products along a wall or table; travel beside a walking character in an opening or transition.
moves.prompt_phrase: camera trucks left sideways on a dolly, sliding past the subject, strong parallax in the foreground

ai_risk.note: Lateral parallax is well supported. Foreground objects can morph at the frame edge and lateral distance errors skew scale. Keep one direction and one speed; pick left or right, not both. One camera move per clip only.

preset.label: TRANSITION_LATERAL_TRUCK
preset.prompt: camera trucks left sideways on a dolly, sliding past the subject, one camera move only

moves.name: Drone fly-in
moves.what_it_is: Signature drone: aerial camera flies in over the landscape toward the subject or location, dropping scale from vast to intimate in one continuous move.
moves.emotion: Arrival, spectacle, welcome, the world opening up for the story.
moves.use_when: Open the whole video or open a scene on a sweeping aerial approach.
moves.prompt_phrase: sweeping drone fly-in, aerial camera flying forward over the landscape toward the subject

ai_risk.note: Fast flight warps terrain and smears the ground; keep it slow and the landscape simple. The subject can morph at close range and scale can drift on the approach, so end the move before reaching a face. One camera move per clip only.

preset.label: OPEN_DRONE_FLY_IN
preset.prompt: sweeping drone fly-in, slow aerial camera flying forward over a simple landscape toward the subject, one camera move only

moves.name: Aerial reveal
moves.what_it_is: Signature drone: aerial camera rises or crests to uncover a hidden location, crowd or scale that was blocked from the low view.
moves.emotion: Awe, geography, 'how big this really is'.
moves.use_when: Reveal a place, a crowd or the true scale at a scene transition or a key turn.
moves.prompt_phrase: aerial drone reveal, camera rising to uncover the vast location below

ai_risk.note: The uncovered area is invented, so keep it simple and keep the rise slow to limit terrain morphing. One camera move per clip only Watch for scale errors.

preset.label: TRANSITION_AERIAL_REVEAL
preset.prompt: aerial drone reveal, slow camera rise uncovering a simple vast location, one camera move only

moves.name: Ascending drone
moves.what_it_is: Signature drone: camera climbs straight up on a drone, lifting from subject height to a high aerial, trading intimacy for geography.
moves.emotion: Release, grandeur, leaving the small problem for the big picture.
moves.use_when: Close a scene by lifting away; hand off from an intimate beat to a wide world.
moves.prompt_phrase: drone ascending straight up, camera rising from the subject to a high aerial view

ai_risk.note: Scale errors as the subject shrinks fast; the ground can morph. Keep the climb slow and steady. One camera move per clip only.

preset.label: CLOSE_DRONE_ASCEND
preset.prompt: drone ascending straight up, slow steady climb from the subject to a high aerial, one camera move only

moves.name: Descending drone
moves.what_it_is: Signature drone: camera drops from a high aerial down toward the subject, narrowing the world onto one person or place.
moves.emotion: Focus closing in, destiny, the net tightening, arrival.
moves.use_when: Open a scene by dropping onto the subject; set up a confrontation.
moves.prompt_phrase: drone descending from a high aerial down toward the subject, slow controlled drop

ai_risk.note: Subject can morph and scale can drift as the camera closes. Keep the descent slow and stop before the face. One camera move per clip only.

preset.label: OPEN_DRONE_DESCEND
preset.prompt: drone descending from a high aerial down toward the subject, slow controlled drop, one camera move only

moves.name: Drone orbit
moves.what_it_is: Signature drone: aerial camera arcs around the subject, circling to show it from shifting angles against the landscape.
moves.emotion: Importance, hero status, romance, rising tension.
moves.use_when: Hero product, a kiss, a pivotal reveal. Half an orbit at most.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow aerial drone orbit, camera arcing around the subject in a half circle

ai_risk.note: Changing angles demand consistent 3D and often morph the subject or warp the horizon. Use a half orbit at most, a simple subject and a clear background. Fast orbits fail outright; build whip-fast spins as an edit transition, never a single generated move. One camera move per clip only Watch for scale errors.

preset.label: REVEAL_DRONE_ORBIT
preset.prompt: slow aerial drone orbit, camera arcing around the subject in a half circle, simple subject, one camera move only

moves.name: Drone fly-over
moves.what_it_is: Signature drone: aerial camera travels over a place at height, sweeping the landscape without locking onto one subject.
moves.emotion: Freedom, awe, geography, spectacle, connective tissue between places.
moves.use_when: Open a story or bridge two locations in a transition.
moves.prompt_phrase: slow aerial drone fly-over, camera travelling forward over the landscape at height

ai_risk.note: Fast flight warps terrain; keep it slow. One camera move per clip only Watch for subject or terrain morphing and scale errors.

preset.label: OPEN_DRONE_FLY_OVER
preset.prompt: slow aerial drone fly-over, camera travelling forward over a simple landscape, one camera move only

moves.name: Drone pull-back reveal
moves.what_it_is: Signature drone: camera pulls back and up away from the subject on a drone, so the subject shrinks as the surrounding world floods into frame.
moves.emotion: Perspective, smallness, hope or isolation depending on the beat.
moves.use_when: Close the video or a scene by pulling back from the subject to the wider world.
moves.prompt_phrase: drone pull-back reveal, camera pulling back and up away from the subject, the wider world opening around them

ai_risk.note: The world that floods in is invented; scale can error as the subject shrinks. Keep it slow and simple. One camera move per clip only Watch for subject or terrain morphing.

preset.label: CLOSE_DRONE_PULL_BACK_REVEAL
preset.prompt: drone pull-back reveal, slow camera pulling back and up away from the subject, simple world opening around them, one camera move only

moves.name: Drone push-in
moves.what_it_is: Signature drone: camera starts on a wide establishing aerial and pushes in down toward the subject, carrying the whole scale of the world into one person or product.
moves.emotion: Significance, 'this one thing matters inside all of this', focus and importance.
moves.use_when: Open a scene or the whole video from a wide establishing view and drive down onto the subject.
moves.prompt_phrase: drone push-in from a wide establishing aerial down to the subject, slow descent and approach

ai_risk.note: Scale errors and subject morphing as the camera closes on a face or product. Keep the push slow and stop short of the face. One camera move per clip only.

preset.label: OPEN_DRONE_PUSH_IN
preset.prompt: drone push-in from a wide establishing aerial down to the subject, slow descent and approach, one camera move only

lenses.name: 14mm ultra-wide
lenses.what_it_is: About 104 degrees horizontal on full frame. Strong edge stretch and foreground exaggeration.
lenses.use_when: Extreme establishing, tight interiors, stylised action.
lenses.prompt_phrase: shot on a 14mm ultra-wide lens, strong perspective

ai_risk.note: Edge distortion is exaggerated by the model; faces near edges stretch.

lenses.name: 24mm wide
lenses.what_it_is: About 74 degrees. Expansive but more controlled; environmental portraits.
lenses.emotion: Presence in a place; handheld realism.
lenses.use_when: Establishing, action coverage, dialogue in tight spaces.

ai_risk.note: Good for environments.

lenses.name: 35mm
lenses.what_it_is: About 54 degrees. Natural, subject in context.
lenses.prompt_phrase: shot on a 35mm lens, natural perspective

ai_risk.note: The best single default for AI 'cinematic' wide-medium.

lenses.name: 50mm normal
lenses.what_it_is: About 40 degrees. Neutral perspective close to human vision.

ai_risk.note: Safe.

lenses.name: 85mm short tele
lenses.what_it_is: About 24 degrees. Flattering compression, easy shallow focus.
lenses.prompt_phrase: shot on an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, background compressed

ai_risk.note: Strong, widely used in prompts for beautiful portraits.

lenses.name: 135mm tele
lenses.prompt_phrase: shot on a 135mm telephoto lens, compressed background

ai_risk.note: Model approximates; effect is mostly blur plus tight framing.

lenses.name: 200mm long tele
lenses.what_it_is: About 10 degrees. Strongest compression of the set.
lenses.prompt_phrase: shot on a 200mm telephoto lens, extreme compression

ai_risk.note: Same as 135mm.

apertures.name: f/1.4
apertures.what_it_is: Extremely shallow focus, very soft background.
apertures.prompt_phrase: shot at f/1.4, very shallow depth of field, creamy background blur

ai_risk.note: F-stop numbers act as style cues, not literal optics; 'shallow depth of field' is the more reliable phrase.

apertures.name: f/2.8
apertures.prompt_phrase: shot at f/2.8, shallow depth of field

ai_risk.note: Same note.

apertures.name: f/4
apertures.prompt_phrase: shot at f/4, moderate depth of field

ai_risk.note: Same note.

apertures.name: f/5.6
apertures.prompt_phrase: shot at f/5.6, balanced depth of field

ai_risk.note: Same note.

apertures.name: f/8
apertures.what_it_is: Deeper focus; foreground and background hold together.
apertures.prompt_phrase: shot at f/8, deep focus, sharp throughout

ai_risk.note: Use 'deep focus, everything sharp'.

apertures.name: f/11
apertures.prompt_phrase: shot at f/11, deep focus landscape, sharp foreground to horizon

ai_risk.note: Same note.

apertures.name: f/16
apertures.what_it_is: Deepest practical focus; diffraction softness can start.
apertures.prompt_phrase: shot at f/16, deep focus, everything sharp

ai_risk.note: Same note.

lens_looks.name: Anamorphic
lens_looks.what_it_is: Lens that squeezes the image; widescreen 2.39:1 with oval bokeh and horizontal flares.
lens_looks.prompt_phrase: anamorphic lens, 2.39:1 widescreen, oval bokeh, horizontal blue lens flare

ai_risk.note: Style cue; Runway guidance explicitly encourages it; do not combine with a conflicting aspect ratio.

lens_looks.name: Lens flare
lens_looks.what_it_is: Streaks or ghosting when bright light hits the lens.
lens_looks.use_when: Backlit sunsets, car lights, stylised scenes.
lens_looks.prompt_phrase: subtle lens flare from the setting sun behind the subject

ai_risk.note: Easy; overuse hides detail.

lens_looks.name: Bokeh
lens_looks.what_it_is: Quality of out-of-focus highlights; strongest at wide apertures.
lens_looks.prompt_phrase: shallow depth of field with soft round bokeh in the background

ai_risk.note: Reliable.

grammar.what: Keep the camera on one side of the line between two subjects so left-right positions stay constant across cuts.
grammar.if_broken: Characters appear to swap sides; confusion.
grammar.prompt_tip: Per scene, fix 'A on the left facing right, B on the right facing left' and repeat that text in every prompt.

grammar.what: A character's look direction should match between shots so the glance seems to land on the other person.
grammar.if_broken: Characters seem to look past each other.
grammar.prompt_tip: State 'looking toward the right of frame' in A's prompt and 'looking toward the left of frame' in B's.

grammar.what: Keep movement in a consistent left-to-right or right-to-left direction across cuts.
grammar.prompt_tip: Write 'walking left to right' in every shot of the same journey.

grammar.what: Cut during a movement so the next shot continues it.
grammar.prompt_tip: Start the next clip at the same pose the previous ended on; use the last frame as the start image.

grammar.what: Alternate between two opposing views of the speakers, respecting the 180-degree line.
grammar.if_broken: Speakers seem not to face each other.
grammar.prompt_tip: Use over-the-shoulder pairs with mirrored framing and same lens.

grammar.what: Shoot the scene wide first, then closer shots to cut between.
grammar.if_broken: No geography, no way to hide errors.
grammar.prompt_tip: Generate the master first; every later shot reuses its location and wardrobe text.

grammar.what: Open each scene with a wide shot that places the audience.
grammar.prompt_tip: First shot of every scene is an extreme wide or wide.

grammar.what: Place the subject on grid lines or intersections.
grammar.prompt_tip: Say 'subject on the left third of the frame'.

grammar.what: Space above the head; too little cramps, too much shrinks.
Space in front of a gaze or movement.
grammar.prompt_tip: Say 'space in front of her, looking into the frame'.

grammar.what: Roads, walls, shadows pointing to the subject.
grammar.prompt_tip: Say 'converging road leads the eye to the subject'.
Say 'foreground branches out of focus, subject in midground, mountains in background'.

grammar.what: Subject seen through a doorway or window.
grammar.prompt_tip: Say 'seen through a doorway, framed by the door'.

top_rules: Open every scene with an establishing wide or extreme wide; never open on a close-up.
Cap close-ups and extreme close-ups at 30 percent of shots (25 percent for drama); make medium the largest share.
One camera move per clip, one subject action per clip, 4-6 seconds each.
Default to static or slow push-in; promote to tracking, pan, tilt or crane only for a stated reason.
Never request whip pans, fast orbits or dolly zoom in a single clip; build whip pans as an edit transition.
Never place two consecutive shots at the same size; jump at least two steps (wide to medium close-up, medium to wide).
Alternate angle family every two to three shots: eye level baseline, low for power, high for vulnerability, overhead for geography.
Every dialogue scene gets a master or two-shot, then over-the-shoulder pairs, then one close-up at the emotional peak only.
Lock the 180-degree line, screen direction and left-right positions in text and repeat them in every prompt of the scene.
Put shot size first in the prompt, then angle, then the single move with speed, then subject, lens look, lighting.
Keep hands, text and logos large or off-screen; add text and logos in post.
Give each shot a job (orient, move, emphasise, react, release) and end sequences on a wide pull-back or reveal.

move_distinction.dolly: A dolly move physically moves the camera through space, so foreground and background shift against one another and the shot gains real parallax and depth.
move_distinction.zoom: A zoom only changes the lens focal length; the camera stays put, so there is no parallax and the background optically compresses toward the subject.
move_distinction.why_it_matters: Models routinely collapse the two. Ask for a dolly when you want parallax, depth and 'entering the space'. Ask for a zoom when you want flat optical magnification without the camera moving. The dolly zoom is the deliberate combination of both and is the hardest of the three to generate reliably.
move_distinction.test_per_model: Kling and Veo guidance disagree on how each model separates a dolly from a zoom and how reliably it honours the distinction, so every dolly-versus-zoom move is marked test_per_model true and must be verified per model before it is trusted in a shot list.

signature_families.note: Signature moves the planner may drop at the start of a scene or the whole video. Each carries a preset. Every move is test_per_model because Kling and Veo sources disagree.
